posts.content_md:
Hi, does anyone know of a UK supplier of the JD-2 bleaching chemicals:

 Potassium Dichromate 5 grams

 Sodium Bisulfate 80 grams

Since developer A & B are mixed when used, I get twice as much ab as bleach. If I could just buy these 2 chemicals and get more bleach then it would all go twice as far.

Any help would be ACE. thanks, Rick.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Even though you have twice as much developer (A + B), the bleach should still outlast your developer. When I was using Potassium Dichromate bleach I would reuse it over and over again. It usually outlasted the developer. Make sure your rinse between devoper and bleach is running water and of addequate time. When I was doing 4 x 5 plates I would make up the bleach and divide it into 2 - 500ml bottles. I only needed 500 ml in the tray at a time. Then when one bottle was exausted, many holograms later, I would use the second 500ml bottle.

Are you discarding the bleach with the developer?

Sorry if this doesn't answer your question directly.

posts.author: rja4096
posts.content_md:
John,

Thanks, that does answer my question. I had been discarding the bleach after every use. Do you know if it is ok to reuse the A + B developer a couple of times too? (for JD-2)

Thanks, Rick.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
From what I understand the mixed A and B have a shelf life of 8 hours but every time you develop a hologram in it, it changes it's characteristics and you will have to alter your developing times and procedures. So in my opinion, anytime you have a two part developer, mix just enough A and B to develop a single hologram then discard. If you use a tray that is just slightly larger then the hologram (hard plastic sandwich containers are good) then minimal liquid is needed. I think I used to used 50ml A and 50ml B for a 4 x 5 glass holographic plate which yielded enough for 20 plates I could develop.

For the bleach, as I stated I used 500ml and would use it until it stopped bleaching in under 2 minutes. When done with the bleach for a single session I would simply but it back in a 500ml container and use it again the next time. Most of the time the bleach would last a good 40 plates. I would NOT recommend trying to use 100ml of the bleach and then put it back into the other 400 or 900ml. I would use 500ml or 1 liter all at once.

TIP: Here are collapsible bottles which I use. I don't think the developers (A and B) need to be kept air free but I use these probably from a left over discipline from Black and White Photography processing.

[http://www.danmassey.co.uk/darkroom/Fil ... pment3.htm](http://www.danmassey.co.uk/darkroom/Film_processing_Equipment3.htm)

Here is another very good reference to processing chemicals and procedures. The JD2 processing has addition information then that on Integraf's instructions. For one, Integraf does not tell you the shelf life of the mixed A and B. Maybe I missed it, but I could not find it. Photography Formula’s paper on JD2 does present this limitation. Do a search on "JD" and you will find the JD2 paper. Also, it reinforces what I stated about the bleach.

[http://www.photoformulary.com/DesktopDe ... 4&tabid=23](http://www.photoformulary.com/DesktopDefault.aspx?tabindex=4&tabid=23)

Anyone using first hand this developer and bleach please chime in with additional information pertaining to experience, corrections or advice.

Peace!

PS: Colin, maybe we should contact Integraf and have them add the notes to their instructions on the amount of A and B to use, the shelf life of the A and B mixed, how to use the bleach (all at once), and the shelf life/exhaustion point of the used bleach.

well almost, anyway...

My first batch of JD-2 bleach lasted over a year, at least 80 holograms. I lost volume to the rinses, but it still worked, if just slower. I'd say you can use it till it's gone.
